scenes.brief: Commissioning week. 20LFB10CF002 (feed flow controller on 20LFB10AA101) keeps oscillating because the upstream feed composition swings. Dana decides to deliberately detune 20LFB10CF002 for now rather than chase it. Luis asks if operators should expect sluggish feed response and Dana says yes, that is intentional. Priya makes the tuning change.
Pure shift chatter: who covers Saturday, a coffee machine complaint, a reminder about hard hats in the new unit. Nothing technical.

Morning of the incident. 20LFC20AP001 tripped and smells burnt; Mark found the mechanical seal failed. Luis says 20LFC20BB001 was drained empty overnight: 20LFC20AA102 went fully open during an instrument air pressure dip and emptied the drum, then 20LFC20AP001 ran dry. Dana says come get her, she is heading down, and tells them to run 20LFC20AP002 and keep 20LFC20BB001 level up manually.

Follow-up. Dana confirms root cause: seal failed from dry running after 20LFC20AA102 failed open on the air dip. Priya confirms the air header dipped. Hannah says there will be an incident review meeting and an MOC for corrective actions. They agree a low-low level protection on the reflux pumps is needed.

MOC-2019-021 review. Changes: add low-low level trip 20LFC20CL101 on both reflux pumps (20LFC20AP001 and 20LFC20AP002), add check valves 20LFC20AA011 and 20LFC20AA012 on the pump discharges, and add a low-flow alarm 20LFC20CF101. Hannah asks about proof testing, Luis asks what operators will see when the trip fires. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 1.
Chatter about a contractor parking issue, a forklift near-miss reminder, and the cafeteria menu. Nothing technical.

MOC-2020-014: upsize the trim on 20LFC20AA101 (reflux control valve) from Cv 45 to Cv 75 because the plant is moving to higher feed rates and the old trim runs out of range. Hannah asks about noise and cavitation, Dana says it is fine at the new rates. Priya will update the valve datasheet. Approved, Rev 2.

Since the 20LFC20AA101 trim change, the valve hunts whenever the unit runs below about 40% load. Luis says operators now put 20LFC20CF002 in manual below 40% and nudge it by hand. Dana says that is a known side effect of the bigger trim and not worth another change right now.

Mark says the 20LFC20AP001 seal was replaced again, work order WO-71120. He suspects shaft misalignment this time, not dry running. Dana agrees it looks like alignment and says make 20LFC20AP002 the preferred duty pump and keep 20LFC20AP001 as standby. Luis updates the operator notes.

Hannah mentions that after the inspection group re-evaluated the column MAWP, 20LFC10AA191 set pressure was lowered from 17.2 to 16.5 barg. Priya asks whether the PSV datasheet in Drive has been updated, Hannah says she has not gotten to it yet. Dana says just remember the drawing still says 17.2 until someone fixes it. Do NOT mention approvals, MOC or paperwork for the change.
Chatter: a lunch order, shift swap request, a forklift beeping complaint. Nothing technical.

20LFB20AC001 (feed/bottoms exchanger) is fouling and feed temperature to the column is sagging. Luis says operators keep chasing it. Dana says she will propose a bypass around 20LFB20AC001 so they can hold feed temperature between cleanings. Mark says cleanings are expensive so a bypass buys time.

MOC-2022-007: add bypass valve 20LFB20AA001 around 20LFB20AC001 to hold feed temperature as the exchanger fouls. Hannah asks about overheating downstream, Dana says operators open it partially and watch the bottoms temperature. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 3.

Evening shift tripped 20LFD10CT101, the high-temperature alarm on the storage tank, after opening 20LFB20AA001 all the way. Luis explains that with the bypass open the bottoms run hotter on their way to storage, and 20LFD10CT101 trips at 55 C. Dana says never fully open 20LFB20AA001, only crack it and watch the storage temperature. Mark says he will add a note to the operator sheet.

MOC-2023-009: relocate 20LFC30CT001 from tray 28 to tray 32 and raise 20LFC30CT002 setpoint from 78 to 81 C, with a loop retune. Hannah asks if the new setpoint stays inside product spec, Dana says yes. Approved, Rev 4.

After moving 20LFC30CT001 to tray 32, Priya says the old tray 28 reading was insensitive, which is why they moved it; the new location responds much faster. She finished the retune of 20LFC30CT002 and the loop is stable at 81 C. Dana says good, tell Luis's crew the old setpoint was 78 in case they see it in old notes.
Chatter: summer heat, a broken break-room fridge, a reminder about a safety stand-down. Nothing technical.

Mark says 20LFB20AC001 was cleaned last week. He reminds everyone the cleaning interval is about 18 months and the last cleaning before this one was why 20LFB20AA001 had been open so much. Luis says feed temperature is back to normal and 20LFB20AA001 is closed again.

Near-miss during startup. Luis says 20LFC20BB001 nearly overfilled because 20LFC20CL002 was left in manual and nobody caught it until the high level alarm. Mark says he saw level climbing and called it in. They agree nobody was hurt and nothing was released, but it was close. Luis says there will be a review.

Review of the near-miss. Dana says 20LFC20AA102 currently fails open, which is part of why the drum can overfill when the controller is out of the loop. She proposes changing 20LFC20AA102 to fail closed, accepting the overfill risk because the high-level alarm covers it. Hannah wants it done under an MOC. Priya will check the actuator.

MOC-2024-031: change 20LFC20AA102 fail position from fail-open to fail-closed. The overfill risk is accepted and covered by the high-level alarm. Luis asks how operators will know the valve closed on loss of air. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 5.

During a preventive maintenance round Priya found the 20LFC20AA102 actuator is still set up fail-open, even though the drawing and the MOC say fail-closed. She raised work order WO-88213 to fix it. Dana says that should have been done when the MOC closed and asks Priya to chase it. The conversation ends with no one confirming it got done.
Mostly chatter and scheduling. Somewhere in it Mark says the steam trap on 20LFC30AC001 is not great but has never failed, so he is not planning to touch it. Do not explain why or give any sizing.

A new operator asked Luis about starting the reflux pumps. Dana repeats her rule: never start either reflux pump unless 20LFC20BB001 level is at least 30%. Luis says he will add it to the startup checklist. Dana mentions she is putting together handover notes in Drive before she retires.

Dana's last day. Warm farewell chatter. Luis thanks her, Mark jokes about her rules of thumb, Priya says the handover notes are in Drive but she knows they are not complete. Dana says ask Priya and Luis, they know where things are buried. No new technical facts.
